claims.text: A thin nanocrystalline alumina coating deposited by atomic layer deposition on zirconium-alloy cladding will improve high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The alumina coating will act as a diffusion barrier against oxygen.
The alumina coating will not compromise the cladding's service suitability.
Atomic layer deposition can produce a uniform, approximately 50 nm alumina coating with excellent conformality and thickness control on the cladding surface.
The deposited alumina layer will be dense, nanocrystalline, continuous, and adherent.
A dense, continuous alumina layer will reduce oxygen diffusion into the zirconium alloy.
Alumina limits oxygen transport by forming a stable, slow-growing oxide barrier.
Limiting oxygen transport will reduce the exothermic oxidation reaction rate of the underlying zirconium alloy.
An approximately 50 nm coating is thin enough to maintain the neutron transparency required for service.
An approximately 50 nm coating is thin enough to maintain the mechanical integrity required for service.
After exposure at 1200 °C for 1 hour in an air/steam environment, alumina-coated cladding will have lower oxidation weight gain than uncoated cladding.
After the same exposure, alumina-coated cladding will have a thinner oxide scale than uncoated cladding.
The coated cladding will retain its mechanical properties and neutron transmission properties relative to uncoated cladding.
Uncoated zirconium-alloy cladding typically exhibits higher oxidation rates under high-temperature air/steam conditions than the proposed coated cladding.
The proposed oxidation-resistance benefit is expected to hold at temperatures up to approximately 1200 °C for alumina coatings approximately 50 nm thick.
Substantial deviations from a 50 nm coating thickness may alter the coating's effectiveness or compromise cladding performance.
Exposure well above 1200 °C may alter the coating's effectiveness or compromise cladding performance.
Repeated thermal cycling may impair long-term alumina-coating adherence.
Neutron irradiation may affect coating integrity and cladding performance during prolonged service.
